content.title: Complete an existing incomplete task from the list
content.intent: Prove that clicking an existing incomplete task's checkbox marks that task complete and shows the completed presentation.
content.technique_notes: Techniques judged: equivalence partitioning applicable because the source grounded one meaningful input state — an existing incomplete task with a clickable checkbox — and no outcome-changing partitions beyond that state were specified. Boundary value analysis not applicable because the use-case stated no numeric, ordered, or length-constrained input. Negative/error not minted because the source did not define invalid input, blocked completion, or failure semantics for this action. Auth, CRUD round-trip, idempotency, concurrency, pagination, i18n, a11y, responsiveness, and performance were not applicable from the evidence because the PRD only promised a local UI state change and visual styling on completion. Budget ceiling present (max_pairs=8); 1 candidate scenario fit within the ceiling, so no scenario was evicted.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Scored highest because it is the only source-grounded journey that exercises both promised outcomes: the completed state and the strikethrough presentation.

[self_critique] Checked for omitted boundary, negative, and toggle-back journeys. Did not mint them because the source did not specify reversibility, error handling, limits, or alternate surfaces for this use-case, so adding them would have invented behavior.
